communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In one sentence: this request asks how the Department of Attorney General handled consumer complaints about a Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit calculation error in Intuit Inc.'s tax software, what it asked Intuit, what it told consumers, and whether it opened an inquiry.

Context, from public sources. Intuit Inc. states on its TurboTax support site, in the article "Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit, Tax Year 2022", that "Some Michigan TurboTax customers have overpaid their state taxes due to an error with the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit," and stated on its ProSeries community board on April 23, 2024 that the Michigan EITC calculation was incorrect for part-year resident filers in its tax year 2022 and 2023 Michigan programs, with corrections released March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024. Records released by the Department of Treasury under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026 show that Intuit informed Treasury of the issue on March 13, 2024 and that Treasury answered on March 20, 2024 that affected taxpayers would need to file amended returns. A consumer complaint concerning the issue was referred by the Department of Attorney General to Treasury's Bureau of Tax Policy on or about May 7, 2026.

Definitions. "The Issue" means the eligibility for, or computation of, the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit for part-year resident or nonresident filers in tax preparation software distributed by Intuit Inc. (TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect or Lacerte), including the corrections Intuit released on March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024. "Intuit" means Intuit Inc., its subsidiaries, employees, agents and counsel, including any address at intuit.com. "The Department" means the Department of Attorney General, including the Consumer Protection Team and any other division or bureau. "Communications" includes email with attachments, letters, meeting notes, memoranda, and entries in any complaint or case management system. Unless an item states otherwise, the period is January 1, 2022 through the date of your search.

Not requested: the text of complaints or attachments submitted by consumers. This request is for the Department's own records of what it did.

Records requested, in order of priority:

1. Count and log. An existing count, log extract, or list of complaint numbers, receipt dates and dispositions for consumer complaints received by the Department from January 1, 2020 through the date of your search that concern Intuit's TurboTax or ProSeries software and the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit, with complainants' personal identifying information redacted.

2. What the Department told consumers. The Department's outgoing acknowledgments, responses, closing letters and referral letters on those complaints, and any template or form response used for them, with complainants' personal identifying information redacted.

3. What the Department asked Intuit, and what Intuit said. All communications between the Department and Intuit concerning the Issue, including any inquiry the Department sent, any response, and any information Intuit supplied about the number of affected Michigan customers, notification of customers, refunds or amended returns, with complainants' names and contact details redacted.

4. Referrals to Treasury. All records of the referral of any complaint or inquiry concerning the Issue to the Department of Treasury, including the referral to Treasury's Bureau of Tax Policy on or about May 7, 2026, any response received from Treasury, and any further action taken or decided, excluding the complainant's own submission and attachments and with the complainant's name and contact details redacted.

5. Whether an inquiry was opened. Records reflecting whether the Department opened, declined to open, or closed any inquiry or investigation under the Michigan Consumer Protection Act, MCL 445.901 et seq., or otherwise, concerning the Issue, including intake or evaluation memoranda, closing memoranda, and any notice to Intuit. If the Department withholds investigating records, please release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244 and describe what is withheld, including the dates on which any inquiry was opened and closed.

6. Press, legislative and public inquiries. Records of inquiries to the Department from the press, from members of the Legislature, or from the public concerning the Issue, and the Department's responses, including any public statement the Department prepared or issued.

Format. Under MCL 15.234(1)(c), please provide the records electronically, as native email files (.eml or .msg) with attachments where they exist, otherwise as searchable PDF.

Fees. I ask that the Department waive or reduce fees under MCL 15.234(2). The records concern the Department's handling of consumer complaints about a software vendor's publicly acknowledged error in a state tax credit for working families with low incomes, and every record released will be published without charge on this public page for anyone to read. I am an individual requester and the request has no commercial purpose. If a fee is charged, please send the detailed itemization required by MCL 15.234(4) before processing. If the estimate exceeds $300, please contact me before doing any work so that I can narrow the request, and in any case please process the items in the order listed. Any deposit is limited to half of the estimate under MCL 15.234(8).

If any part is denied, please cite the specific exemption for each record or portion, release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244, and describe what is withheld. Please respond within the 5 business days provided by MCL 15.235(2).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Burak Genc

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In one sentence: this request asks how the Department of Treasury approves and tests tax preparation software for Michigan returns, what its e-file Business Rule 74 has said since 2013, and what it told software developers before and after Intuit Inc. corrected its Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit calculation for part-year residents in 2024.

Context, from public sources. Intuit stated on its ProSeries community board on April 23, 2024 that the Michigan EITC calculation was incorrect for part-year resident filers in its tax year 2022 and 2023 Michigan programs, with corrections released March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024, and its TurboTax support site states that "Some Michigan TurboTax customers have overpaid their state taxes due to an error with the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit." Treasury records released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026 show that Treasury's e-file Business Rule 74 was based on an April 2, 2012 Treasury memorandum and that its logic had not been updated since tax year 2013. Treasury's software developer page states that every developer producing Michigan tax preparation software must complete Form 4430, the Michigan Letter of Intent to Participate in E-File and Substitute Forms Programs.

Definitions. "Intuit" means Intuit Inc., its subsidiaries, employees, agents and counsel, including any address at intuit.com. "Intuit's Michigan products" means TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect and Lacerte as used to prepare Michigan individual income tax returns. "Communications" includes email with attachments, letters, memoranda, bulletins, and messages in any ticketing or case system.

Records requested, in order of priority:

1. Approval and testing of Intuit's Michigan products, tax years 2021 through 2025. Form 4430 submissions by Intuit; Treasury's approval, acceptance, rejection or conditional-approval communications for Intuit's Michigan individual income tax products; test package results, and any test scenario, for returns of part-year residents claiming the Michigan EITC; any notice of error, defect or correction that Intuit submitted to Treasury; and any suspension, revocation or corrective-action correspondence. Where a record contains confidential commercial information, please release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244.

2. Business Rule 74. The text of Business Rule 74 as published to software developers for each of tax years 2013 through 2025; any change log or version history; and the records of the March 2024 internal review in which Individual Income Tax management concurred that the rule's logic remained applicable, including the two messages released on August 11, 2026 and anything beyond them.

3. Notices to all software developers. Bulletins, memoranda, test-package changes, or messages to the software developer distribution list concerning Michigan EITC eligibility or computation for part-year or nonresident filers, from January 1, 2022 through the date of your search, including anything issued after March 7, 2024. Documents currently posted on Treasury's public software developer site may be excluded if you identify each excluded document by title and date.

4. All-vendor counts. Any existing aggregate record of Business Rule 74 rejection counts for all software vendors, or for vendors other than Intuit, by processing year, without identifiers, product names or taxpayer-specific facts. I am not asking Treasury to create a record; if no such existing record is retained, please state that in the response.

5. Who else has asked. The entries in Treasury's FOIA request log or tracking system for requests received from January 1, 2024 through the date of your search that concern Intuit, TurboTax, ProSeries or the Michigan EITC, with requesters' personal information redacted.

Records released previously. The April 2, 2012 memorandum "MI EITC and nonresidents" and the "EIC Question" messages of March 6 and 7, 2024 were released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026. Please include them again in response to item 2, so that the public record on this page is complete.

Custodians and search terms. Forms, Documentation and E-file Services, including MIFormsEfile@michigan.gov and the staff who administer the software developer program; the Tax Processing Bureau; Individual Income Tax Division management; the FOIA Coordinator's office; and Heather Vellanti and Scott Bunnells, whom Treasury's released records identify. Suggested search terms: Intuit, TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect, Lacerte, "Form 4430", "letter of intent", "test package", ATS, EITC, EIC, "earned income", "part-year", nonresident, "Business Rule 74", BR74.

Format. Under MCL 15.234(1)(c), please provide the records electronically, as native email files (.eml or .msg) with attachments where they exist, otherwise as searchable PDF.

Fees. I ask that Treasury waive or reduce fees under MCL 15.234(2). The records concern how the state approves the software that prepares most Michigan returns and how a publicly acknowledged calculation error in a credit for working families with low incomes passed through that process, and every record released will be published without charge on this public page for anyone to read. I am an individual requester and the request has no commercial purpose. If a fee is charged, please send the detailed itemization required by MCL 15.234(4) before processing. If the estimate exceeds $300, please contact me before doing any work so that I can narrow the request, and in any case please process the items in the order listed. Any deposit is limited to half of the estimate under MCL 15.234(8).

If any part is denied, please cite the specific exemption for each record or portion, release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244, and describe what is withheld. Please respond within the 5 business days provided by MCL 15.235(2).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

In one sentence: this request asks for the Department of Treasury's records of what Intuit Inc. told the state about a Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit calculation error affecting part-year residents who used its tax software, and what the state decided to do for the taxpayers affected.

Context, from public sources. Intuit Inc. states on its TurboTax support site, in the article "Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit, Tax Year 2022", that "Some Michigan TurboTax customers have overpaid their state taxes due to an error with the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit," and stated on its ProSeries community board on April 23, 2024 that the Michigan EITC calculation was incorrect for part-year resident filers in its tax year 2022 and 2023 Michigan programs, with corrections released March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024. Treasury's own records, released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026, show that Intuit informed Treasury of the issue on March 13, 2024, that Treasury answered on March 20, 2024 that affected taxpayers would need to file amended returns, and that Intuit stated the same day that tax year 2022 filers were also affected.

Definitions. "The Issue" means the eligibility for, or computation of, the Michigan Earned Income Tax Credit for part-year resident or nonresident filers in tax preparation software distributed by Intuit Inc. (TurboTax, ProSeries, ProConnect or Lacerte), including Treasury e-file Business Rule 74 and the corrections Intuit released on March 7, 2024 and April 18, 2024. "Intuit" means Intuit Inc., its subsidiaries, employees, agents and counsel, including any address at intuit.com. "Communications" includes email with attachments, letters, meeting notes, memoranda, and messages in any ticketing or case system. Unless an item states otherwise, the period is January 1, 2022 through the date of your search.

Records requested, in order of priority:

1. What Intuit told Treasury in 2024 and since. All communications between Treasury and Intuit concerning the Issue from January 1, 2024 through the date of your search, including the March 2024 threads that Treasury released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026 (please include them again so that the record on this page is complete); any list, count, description or identifiers of affected returns or taxpayers that Intuit supplied; any request by Treasury for such a list; and any communication concerning amended returns, refunds, interest, notification of affected taxpayers, or the corrections Intuit released. Taxpayer identifiers may be redacted.

2. What Treasury decided for affected taxpayers. Records from March 13, 2024 through the date of your search reflecting Treasury's consideration or decision whether affected returns would be adjusted by Treasury or corrected by amended return, and whether affected taxpayers would be notified by Treasury, by Intuit or by anyone, including any decision not to notify; the consultation with Treasury's tax experts referenced on March 19, 2024; any memorandum, legal or policy analysis, or meeting notes; and any draft or issued taxpayer notice, press release or website statement concerning the Issue.

3. The March 2022 exchange. The complete thread of the communications between Treasury and Intuit on or about March 25, 2022 concerning the computation of the Michigan EITC on part-year and nonresident returns with zero taxable income (a portion of which Treasury released on July 28, 2026), including any earlier message that prompted it, Treasury's internal routing or review of it, the records of the instruction, form or publication revisions Treasury indicated it would raise for the following year, and any record showing whether those revisions were made for tax year 2022.

4. The MIFormsEfile mailbox. All communications concerning the Issue in the MIFormsEfile@michigan.gov mailbox from January 1, 2022 through the date of your search. Treasury's August 11, 2026 export of that mailbox was an empty archive, although the mailbox appears as a recipient on at least three released messages. Please also provide the search or export log, manifest or results summary produced by the tool used, and, if the mailbox holds no responsive records, the written no-records statement for it.

5. Any existing count. Any existing report, summary, dashboard, query result summary or analysis, in aggregate form, of (a) amended MI-1040 returns filed on or after March 1, 2024 for tax year 2022 or 2023 that added or increased the Michigan EITC, in total or by software developer; or (b) part-year resident returns for tax year 2022 or 2023 on which a federal EITC was reported and no Michigan EITC was claimed. I am not asking Treasury to create a record or to run a new query. If no such existing record exists, please state that in the response.

6. Who was told. Records from March 1, 2024 through the date of your search by which Treasury informed or briefed the State Treasurer's office, the Governor's office, any member or committee of the Legislature or the House or Senate Fiscal Agency, the Department of Attorney General, or any news organization about the Issue, including media inquiries and Treasury's responses; and Treasury's records of its handling of the consumer complaint concerning TurboTax's Michigan EITC calculation that the Department of Attorney General referred to Treasury's Bureau of Tax Policy on or about May 7, 2026, including any inquiry to Intuit and any response to the Attorney General, but excluding the complainant's own submission and attachments and with the complainant's name and contact details redacted.

Records released previously. Several responsive records were released under FOIA on July 28 and August 11, 2026: the April 2, 2012 memorandum "MI EITC and nonresidents"; the "EIC Question" thread of March 6 and 7, 2024; the "TurboTax and EITC for PY residents" thread of March 13 to 20, 2024; and two Outlook messages from the VellantiH mailbox. Please include them in this response rather than omitting them, so that the public record on this page is complete; they are already collected and few in number.

Custodians and search terms. Treasury's released records identify these custodians and locations: Forms, Documentation and E-file Services, including MIFormsEfile@michigan.gov; Individual Income Tax Division management; the Tax Policy Bureau, Indirect Taxes Division; the Office of Communications; and Heather Vellanti, Mark Chambers, Cassidy Shankleton, Jennifer Crane, Debra Salisbury and Scott Bunnells. Suggested search terms: Intuit, TurboTax, ProSeries, EITC, EIC, "earned income", "part-year", "PY resident", nonresident, "Business Rule 74", BR74.

Format. Under MCL 15.234(1)(c), please provide the records electronically, as native email files (.eml or .msg) with attachments and metadata where they exist, otherwise as searchable PDF, as Treasury did on August 11, 2026.

Fees. I ask that Treasury waive or reduce fees under MCL 15.234(2). The records concern the state's administration of a refundable credit for working families with low incomes, a software vendor's publicly acknowledged calculation error, and the state's response, and every record released will be published without charge on this public page for anyone to read. If any part is denied, please cite the specific exemption for each record or portion, release the nonexempt portions under MCL 15.244, and describe what is withheld. Please respond within the 5 business days provided by MCL 15.235(2).

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Public Records Request - Forest County Incident Numbers 201400014171, 2011C5793, 2012C2380

Related to: Stephanie A. Low (deceased) / Kristopher P. Torgerson



INTRODUCTION



Pursuant to the Wisconsin Public Records Law, Wis. Stat. §§ 19.31-19.39, I hereby request access to and copies of all records described below. This request is made on behalf of Kristopher Paul Torgerson, for whom I hold Power of Attorney, in connection with ongoing post-conviction proceedings.



The Wisconsin Public Records Law provides that all persons have a right to inspect any record unless otherwise specifically provided by law. Wis. Stat. § 19.35(1)(a). The law presumes complete public access to government records, and any exception to disclosure must be narrowly construed. Wis. Stat. § 19.31.



CASE REFERENCE INFORMATION



Forest County Sheriff's Office Incident Number: 201400014171

Forest County Sheriff's Office Case Number: 2011C5793

Forest County Sheriff's Office Case Number: 2012C2380

Related Wausau PD Case Number: 10-11163

Date of Incident: September 19, 2014

Location: Forest Road 2658, Town of Wabeno, Forest County, Wisconsin

GPS Coordinates: N 45° 23' 18.0204" W 88° 39' 19.6739"

Decedent: Stephanie A. Low

Offense Listed: 940.11(2) - Hiding a Corpse



RECORDS REQUESTED



I request copies of all records in any format (paper, electronic, photographic, video, audio) related to the above-referenced incidents, including but not limited to the following categories:



A. PHOTOGRAPHIC EVIDENCE



Captain Jeff Marvin's report dated September 19, 2014 states: "Lt. Karcz and I did take several pictures during this process." Lt. Andrew Karcz's report confirms he assisted in exhuming the body. I request:



All photographs taken by Lt. Andrew Karcz on September 19, 2014

All photographs taken by Captain Jeff Marvin on September 19, 2014

All photographs taken by any Forest County Sheriff's Office personnel at the scene

All photographs taken during the searches conducted on November 12-13, 2011

All photographs taken during searches conducted on May 16, 2012 and June 30, 2012

Photo logs, metadata, or documentation showing date, time, photographer, and description of each photograph

Chain of custody documentation for all photographic evidence



B. VIDEO EVIDENCE



Wausau Police Department Report 10-11163 (Supplement 0435) references video recording of the scene. I request:



Any and all video recordings made by Forest County Sheriff's Office personnel

Any copies of video recordings received from Wausau Police Department

Any copies of video recordings received from Wisconsin State Crime Laboratory

Body camera or dash camera footage from any Forest County deputies who responded

Video logs or documentation regarding any video evidence



C. COMMUNICATIONS AND CORRESPONDENCE



All emails between Forest County Sheriff's Office and Wausau Police Department regarding this case (2010-2017)

All emails between Forest County Sheriff's Office and Marathon County Medical Examiner

All emails between Forest County Sheriff's Office and Wisconsin State Crime Laboratory

All emails between Forest County Sheriff's Office and National Forest Service LEO Mark Borcovan

All emails between Forest County District Attorney Charles Simono and any parties regarding this case

All written correspondence, letters, memoranda, and faxes related to this case

All text messages or other electronic communications related to this case

Phone logs, call records, or documentation of telephone communications regarding this case



D. MUTUAL AID AND JURISDICTIONAL RECORDS



Lt. Karcz's report references that "Lt. Kolb addressed potential jurisdiction issues with notifications" to Forest County Sheriff John Dennee, Forest County DA Charles Simono, and National Forest Service LEO Mark Borcovan. I request:



The Mutual Aid Agreement fax referenced in Wausau PD Report 10-11163 (Supplement 0217) for November 12-13, 2011 ("2 pages of Forest Co. S.O. Mutual Aid Agreement fax")

Documentation of the "notification" Sheriff Dennee received from Lt. Kolb on September 19, 2014 regarding "jurisdiction issues"

Any written authorization from Sheriff Dennee for Wausau PD to operate in Forest County on September 19, 2014

Any correspondence with U.S. Forest Service regarding jurisdiction or authorization

Any correspondence with Forest County Potawatomi Community regarding searches on tribal land



E. MEDICAL EXAMINER RECORDS



Reports indicate Marathon County Medical Examiner Jessica Blahnick "had contact with Forest County M.E. Larry Mathien, and was given permission to handle the scene." I request:



All records from Forest County Medical Examiner/Coroner Larry Mathein regarding this case

Documentation of any transfer of jurisdiction to Marathon County Medical Examiner

Phone logs, notes, or records of the communication between Larry Mathein and Jessica Blahnick

Any written authorization for Marathon County ME to assume jurisdiction in Forest County

Any Forest County Coroner/ME reports, notes, or determinations regarding this death



F. COMPLETE INVESTIGATION RECORDS



All incident reports, supplemental reports, and narratives for cases 201400014171, 2011C5793, and 2012C2380

All officer notes, field notes, and handwritten documentation

All dispatch records, CAD logs, and radio communications

All evidence logs, property receipts, and chain of custody documentation

Any items collected during the June 30, 2012 search including bone samples, sheet, and prescription bottles

title: Ibrahim Aqil

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Ibrahim Aqil
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I am writing to request records concerning IBRAHIM AQIL, also known as "Tahsin," "Abed Ahmad," and "Abu Suja."
 
This request follows FOIPA Request No. 1647643-000, which the Bureau closed on June 4, 2025, after a standard search of the Central Records System (main and reference entity records)
returned no records responsive to that request. That response invited me to submit "additional information pertaining to the subject of [the] request" so that an additional search could be conducted. This request provides that additional information and asks the Bureau to conduct a new, expanded search on that basis.
 
ADDITIONAL IDENTIFYING AND BACKGROUND INFORMATION
 
Ibrahim Aqil was, until his death, a senior Hezbollah military commander and member of Hezbollah's Jihad Council, and has been publicly linked by the U.S. government to activity squarely within the FBI's counterterrorism mission:
 
  - Aqil was identified by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, in a July 21, 2015 designation under Executive Order 13582, as acting for or on behalf of Hezbollah.
 
  - Aqil was designated by the U.S. Department of State as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist under Executive Order 13224, as amended, effective September 10, 2019.
 
  - The U.S. government's Rewards for Justice program — administered by the State Department in coordination with U.S. law enforcement and intelligence agencies, including the FBI — offered a reward of up to $7 million for information on Aqil.
 
  - Public reporting attributes to Aqil a role, in the early-to-mid 1980s, in the Islamic Jihad Organization cell tied to the April 1983 bombing of the U.S. Embassy in Beirut (63 killed, including 17 Americans) and the October 1983 bombing of the U.S. Marine Corps barracks in Beirut (241 U.S. servicemembers killed) — attacks that were the subject of extensive FBI and U.S. government investigation, and reporting also links him to the taking of American hostages in Lebanon during that period.
 
  - Aqil was reportedly killed in an Israeli airstrike in Beirut on September 20, 2024, an event widely covered in domestic and international press.
 
Given a formal U.S. terrorist designation, a multimillion-dollar federal reward for information on his whereabouts, and his public association with attacks that killed dozens of Americans and prompted a major federal investigation, I believe it is likely that the FBI's Central Records System — including but not limited to files maintained by FBI Headquarters, relevant field offices, and Legal Attaché offices, as well as Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) records — contains records responsive to this request that a standard main-entity-only search would not necessarily surface, particularly reference-entity records connecting Aqil to related investigative files, watch-list or terrorist-designation processing, or the Rewards for Justice program.
 
RECORDS REQUESTED
 
Please search for and produce all records, of any kind, mentioning, referencing, or otherwise relating to Ibrahim Aqil (and the aliases above), including but not limited to:
 
  1. Investigative files, main and reference entity records, indices entries, and 302s or equivalent reports referencing Aqil, under any of the names/aliases listed above;
 
  2. Records relating to Aqil's designation as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist and any predecessate or related Treasury/OFAC designation;
 
  3. Records relating to the Rewards for Justice reward offer concerning Aqil, including any FBI role in vetting, verifying, or acting on tips submitted in connection with that reward;
 
  4. Records relating to the 1983 U.S. Embassy Beirut bombing and/or the 1983 U.S. Marine Corps barracks bombing in Beirut that reference Aqil by name or alias;
 
  5. Any records generated, updated, or closed out following Aqil's reported death on September 20, 2024.
 
INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING SEARCH
 
As required by relevant case law (e.g., Weisberg v. DOJ, 705 F.2d 1344, 1351 (D.C. Cir. 1983); Valencia-Lucena v. U.S. Coast Guard, 180 F.3d 321, 325 (D.C. Cir. 1999)), the FBI must conduct a
search reasonably calculated to uncover all responsive records, including both main and reference entity records given the additional information provided above, and must follow any clear leads it discovers to other systems or record locations. If any potentially responsive records were destroyed, transferred to NARA, or otherwise unavailable, please identify that fact and the applicable disposition authority per FOIPA Addendum Part 1.
 
EXEMPTIONS AND SEGREGABILITY
 
Per the foreseeable-harm standard at 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A), please withhold information only where disclosure would reasonably be expected to harm an interest protected by a specific exemption, or where disclosure is prohibited by law. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of any record, and identify the specific exemption(s) claimed for each redaction or withholding.

FEES AND FORMAT

I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.
